Many among us suffer from this tendency to flee when confronted with something inherently good. This stems from our lack of habituation in witnessing, listening to, and familiarizing ourselves with virtuous matters.

A system known as *Shudranyayam* (the logic of the Shudras) once emerged amidst us. There was an era when a Shudra was prohibited from doing practically anything. They were not allowed to touch, listen, or approach others; if they were to perform any task, they were expected to complete it and immediately run away—this was what they had taught us. Such an oppressive culture prevailed in our society during that period. Subsequently, an opportunity presented itself to the Shudra. This chance materialized in the fourth phase.

It has been 5000 years since the birth of Sree Krishna. During these 5000 years, we have not been able to articulate and realize the true role of the Shudra. By bringing forth great souls into this world, God continuously educates us through their exemplary lives. However, to closely observe and learn from their lives, we require a certain degree of wisdom. It is perhaps due to a deficiency in this wisdom that we have failed to accomplish this.

The Vaishya can conduct himself rather gracefully. Nevertheless, he has been unable to internalize and act upon this higher wisdom. The Marwaris and Gujaratis of Northern India serve as a prime example of this. They are at the forefront not only in generating wealth and sustaining their lives but also in undertaking philanthropic endeavors for various causes. They often execute these acts of charity with immense grandeur. Such behavior is rarely observed among us, as we are unaccustomed to it. When they offer *Gurudakshina*, it is of the highest standard. They continually desire to contribute as much as possible. However, they are equally ruthless in accumulating wealth, harboring no hesitation in adopting any means necessary to acquire it. Ultimately, they gather these riches, only to give them away charitably with the other hand.

Even though kings belonging to the Shudra caste ruled here, it proved futile for us. During the reign of a Shudra, we ought to have attained complete freedom. It was either by divine intervention or a stroke of fortune that administrative power fell into the hands of the Shudras. However, instead of utilizing it for the greater good of the populace, they manipulated it in a manner that exclusively benefited their own kin. They segregated society into various classes and castes, eventually leading to a situation where one Shudra could not even walk in the territory ruled by another Shudra. Consequently, the ruling Shudra began oppressing the other Shudras under the guise of caste divisions. Armed with the scepter of authority, they were prepared to crush anyone who stood in their way. As a direct result of this, they now stand utterly ruined and dismantled. We have failed to perceive this reality. The rest of the Shudras degenerated into a marginalized class devoid of even the right to walk on public roads. It was a dark era when they lacked the fundamental rights to adequate food and clothing. Their garments had to remain strictly above the knee; such was the draconian law. If an official arrived to collect taxes while the head of the household was having a meal, the homeowner had to shout out from his place, stating, "Your humble servant is sitting here drinking a little rice gruel." They were compelled to speak in such a subservient manner. According to the law, when girls attained puberty, four *chakrams* had to be paid to the authorities. Similarly, women were strictly prohibited from covering their breasts. A breast tax, known as *Mulakkaram*, was imposed upon them for this very reason. Failure to pay this tax would result in the authorities confiscating all the decent household goods. Once, when officials visited a house to commit such atrocities, a woman residing there was overcome with unbearable anguish. She placed a fresh plantain leaf before the official, severed the very body parts upon which the tax was levied, and offered them on it. This horrific incident took place in the Cherthala taluk. Even today, recounting this event evokes a profound sense of disgust and horror.

It is only after enduring such an oppressive era that we have arrived at our present state. Thus, the administration of that specific class of Shudras—who subjected us to myriad forms of suffering and actively sought to demean us—has finally been eradicated from this land. Today, even their own descendants cannot justify those past actions. They have evolved to a significantly higher moral standing. That is indeed a blessing. Consequently, we can console ourselves with the hope that some goodness will prevail when they ascend to positions of power.
Guruvani
April 1984

Today, this is not what we need. Today, we have moved far beyond all that and come a long way. However, despite coming this far, we have not been able to achieve what we need. It is not that we have failed to internalize it in our minds. But it is doubtful whether any human being has been able to manifest even a slight change in their behavioral disposition. For instance, an ascetic is unable to do it, and a householder is unable to do it. Then who else can achieve it here? If a householder fails, an ascetic should be able to—and if an ascetic fails, a householder should. Both these groups have failed. Then how can people leading other kinds of lives achieve it? Either the householder should cultivate it themselves, or the ascetic should facilitate it. Both have not materialized. Those we call our ascetics have erred. The householders harbor the misconception that these matters are not for them to practice, but are meant exclusively for a specific group of people. It is as if doing good has been deeded entirely to them. We assume we do not have to do any of this; we can just wander about being bad. We must display foolishness. Seeing all this, we must teach others as well and lead them along this same path. We should be capable of putting on any masquerade for that purpose. We end up demonstrating life in that sense.

What we have heard about people called ascetics is that they at most consume some green leaves. Even then, not all green leaves. An ascetic is one who abstains even from water. That is one group. But I have mentioned this many times before. They achieved this state by consuming poison. Such practices were demonstrated by the royal sages (*Rajarshis*). Seeing his poor subject doing immense good for the people merely with a call to "God," the royal sage felt—this is a terrible predicament, I am being subordinated to him—he pondered over this for a long time. However, there is a way to deceive him. Some ascetics themselves taught him that. What does it mean to consume poison like this? Certain substances belonging to the toxic minerals category (*Pashanas*) are placed inside the stems or at the roots of our cultivated crops as fertilizer. Thus, it is gradually mixed into the food. Today, we experience this even without consciously doing it. It has come to a point where there are no substances without added ammonia. These are being applied to the roots of many plants. Similarly, if poison is continuously ingested in small increments, eventually, consuming a small amount of poison will no longer have any effect.

Thus, among the leaf varieties, it starts with the holy basil leaf and concludes with the *Kanjiram* (poison nut) leaf. It stops at the *Kanjiram* leaf—specifically, its tender shoot. That is referred to as a rejuvenation therapy (*Kalpaseva*). After this come the medicinal varieties. These medicinal herbs do not have the bitterness of the nine toxic minerals (*Navapashana*). Other ingredients apart from *Navapashana* are brought, processed, and consumed as medicine; following this, *Navapashana* itself is purified and ingested. Each has its specific consistency and dosage. After this, there is a combined *Kalpaseva* incorporating everything.

When this stage is reached, he will develop an aversion to food. Then, a very minimal amount of food will suffice for him. Consuming milk, fruits, or similar light diet will be enough. This is what is termed as a prescribed diet. After that, a cave with nine openings or faces is constructed. The stipulation is to spend a specific number of hours at a particular cave entrance. This is done by observing the northern solstice (*Uttarayana*) and southern solstice (*Dakshinayana*). Therefore, during the *Uttarayana* period, one must sit at specific cave entrances. For the next six months, it will be at the *Dakshinayana* entrance. These specific cave openings are constructed only after studying all these factors thoroughly.

After that comes the matter of caretaking. It is said that boys fall short when it comes to caretaking. Girls are better in that regard. Yet, they are easily swayed. They have a disposition where, if they develop an interest, they will act even forgetting their parents. If they place their trust in someone, they will forget everything and follow him. Whatever they are following, they call him their lord. They will simply go after him. So, taking advantage of this convenience, he will win her over. One must be mindful of that too. There are two aspects to what I am saying. Once she is won over, she will remain steadfastly committed to the purpose for which she came. Then, no matter what is offered, she will not turn back. There is no other instrument in this world so unhesitatingly willing to forget the parents who raised them, their locals, and their family. Nevertheless, this is used for that purpose—this is what is called a lawful wife (*Dharmapatni*). Whatever the *Dharma* may be, no matter what, if she is kept close and taught all this, she will look after everything meticulously. By meticulously, it means she will constantly watch to see if there is any deficiency while he is seated. But if he sits, he will slant or fall. Why? Hasn't his body been ruined? This body of his has become completely worthless, like an old rag. Why has it become like a rag? By continuously consuming these three categories, the body has become severely flaccid and distorted. That is a bodily transformation that occurs when consuming this medicine. She will be instructed on the regimen for administering the next medicine to reverse this condition and the protocols for nursing him. She will be taught beforehand exactly what needs to be done. It is after such instruction that she is appointed for caretaking. She will be given some attention and affection. In light of this, she herself will be appointed. Then she will execute this flawlessly.

On the contrary, if a young boy is entrusted with this as a disciple, he will cleverly stand nearby and think, 'When will the Swami wake up next? Let me go and come back in the meantime,' and he will just walk away. Slowly looking back time and again, he will move away and then make a run for it. Even hearing the sound of this running is enough to frighten the ascetic. This has happened to many. These disciples will deceive them like this. But with that, the ascetic's breath (life) will depart. This is something that depends on a fraction of a second. If that precise moment is missed, then everything is ruined; thereafter, neither this food nor medicinal variety will go down his throat. He will die before it even goes inside.

Therefore, it is with all these precautions in mind that a woman is chosen for this. And what if all this is consumed? It is widely believed that all this is a remnant of divine grace. This is nothing divine; it is merely a gimmick he has mastered. Displaying this gimmick, he consumes all this and emerges. It is used over a period of seven years. Six months of regimen, and six months of its preservation. When practiced like this for seven years, seven layers of skin are shed, and truly, aging and greying will not occur. The calculation is that this body can be sustained for about two thousand years. It is brought to this state. The conditions under which this must be achieved have also been written down. This is not called knowledge but rather an attainment (*Siddhi*). Others assume that *Siddhi* means it is bestowed by God. This is not given by God at all.

Because the body is conditioned in this manner, neither food nor water is required thereafter. If any venomous creatures touch him, they will die, but nothing will happen to him. No matter what block of ice he goes and sits on, he remains unaffected. So, seeing all this, we assume—Oh! What a great man he is, while we cannot survive even a single day without water and food. This was devised by the royal sages just to confound the poor common man. Because the Shudra lacked knowledge, he construed this as divine grace. When this Shudra came to rule, many such gimmicks were propagated here.
Guruvani
May 1984

Today, we hold nothing that aligns with the truth. What stands now is a combination of other gimmicks. We ourselves have evidence here that God had a great desire to change this. There were great men and ascetics here who did not employ any such gimmicks. They are the ones who imparted this kind of knowledge to us.

The lore of 'Parayi Petta Panthirukulam' (the twelve lineages born to the Pariah woman) belongs to that category. Except for demonstrating matters concerning certain deities, they did not exhibit any of these gimmicks. They have stated that this system of worship itself is not like this. A proof for that is the idol consecration at the Cherthala Karthyayani Temple. What is known as the Cherthala Pooram takes place there.

All the women who resided in the Buddhist *viharas* were beaten, brought to a place called Kottappuram near Cherai, verbally abused, hacked to death, and thrown into the sea; subsequently, a temple was built there. That is the Kodungallur Bhagavathy Temple. Instead of hacking them to death as was done then, today, goats and fowls are sacrificed. They continue to do this while hurling abuses. It is women who are worshipped there. You can witness all of this if you visit the place. There are several such Devi temples scattered around.

Seeing this and coming down here to South Travancore, we have the 'Mudippura'. Mudippura means - there is no body, only the head, face, and earrings can be seen. They tie it up, plant an arecanut tree trunk in the middle of a paddy field, and tie it to that. Then, when the festival is over, they dismantle it and take it away. This represents the head of a demon. Haven't you seen the figure of Bhadrakali drawn—with several heads of adults and children? It means all of them were chopped off. She stands there holding them hanging in both hands with a sword. She has hands and legs as needed. One hand to hold the sword, one to support the head while cutting it, another to collect the blood, separate hands to hold other weapons, and then separate hands for playing, bathing, and eating. Thus, there are numerous hands. We would be terrified if we look at each of her nails. Their concept is that she will tear things apart with these nails. These are the concepts given to us to worship. What will those who worship this become? If our method of worship takes this path, it is no wonder we perish. It is because our knowledge has perished in this way that we do not hesitate to sacrifice even our own children. You might have read in the newspapers that such sacrifices were made even recently. So, when such things are happening among us, how far do we have to go to progress culturally!

The governance here fell into the hands of the Shudra who had degraded to that level. That governance also degraded the people entirely. Because one group can acquire education, another group cannot; one group can stand close, another group is not allowed to; one group must stand eight *kathams* away, another group can stand one *katham* away. They have contrived to write all this down as *Rajadharma* (royal duty). We must reflect on what all things the 'Ponnuthampran' (sovereign) here has ruled upon in this manner. Then, amidst this, there are the 'Kudiyanavanmar' (feudal lords). They are capable of doing anything. They are the ones ruling the land. When we look at all this, this culture among us has strayed very far away. Then, it is because foreigners like the British or the Arabs came here and made them do things that we achieved the kind of freedom we see here today. Thus, although we lost one *dharma*, we gained another freedom. We got the freedom to walk on the roads, to let others walk, and to get an education. That is why this knowledge could reach India today; otherwise, it would not have.

They give the depressed classes a good name, 'Harijan', but what is done here is gouging out their eyes and dragging them into the fire to burn. He is only ordained to toil for the one who torments him. He has no right to do anything else. If this is what is happening here even in the present situation, how much the people of those times must have suffered! Today, it is claimed that freedom was obtained by these very same groups, yet what we see are the machinations done to deny them freedom. This is what is happening today. We have great freedom to beat people to death. Such great freedom is kept close at hand. This is what is happening today even after we got freedom. Thus, such a subjugated system of governance still exists among us. The things that have befallen us today as a result of such atrocities spreading everywhere throughout the country are called a part of *Kali* (the Kali Yuga). So, what is the special characteristic of *Kali*—it is the time when we all should get freedom. *Kali* has such a merit. That is, not obeying any of these rules. Then poets will emerge, they will write for freedom, they will repeatedly bring about victory in accordance with the times, and that victory will lead to human freedom.

Here itself, so many poets have written with a thirst for freedom. Asan (Kumaran Asan) has also written, urging to change the rules. So, if they say that if you don't change such rules, you will be beaten and destroyed, it will happen just like that. Even though we had an idea to conduct ourselves in a good manner like this, there was no governance here to implement it. We suffer this disability because of that problem. This situation is changing—if not changed, it will come. It will be changed. It will certainly come to be so, without a doubt. But the reason for saying all this in the midst of this is that a section of the people who suffered like this - a society that committed all sorts of atrocities to degrade and destroy humans was prevalent here. As a result of it being prevalent, it became impossible for us even to live here.
Guruvani
June 1984

Prayers related to the full moon (Veluthavavu) have been given great importance among ordinary Hindus since ancient times. After that, we can see that the Arabian people also gave it importance. Buddha has also given it a place. This full moon day has a special quality of good and bad happening equally.

All creation happening on earth takes place with the help of the moon. Without the dust particles of the moon, fertilization will not occur in grains, humans, or other animals. Thus, creation takes place with the help of the moon. It is sustained by the power and heat of the sun. The earth is what comes from the combination of these two. Two phases have been established - the dark phase and the light phase. Great souls, having discovered with divine permission how creation has occurred in this world, have made us understand it.

Hindus have proceeded by attaching a divine concept to everything. For example, they have assigned divinity to the five elements (Panchabhootas). It is done so that humans would respect and practice it. It does not mean they are God. When divinity is assigned, they will be handled without being dismissed or disrespected. Just because they are handled without disrespect, no one should assume that they are God. When we drink water, we drink it thinking of God. Similarly, when a driver drives a vehicle, or a digger takes the spade to dig soil, or a beedi roller takes the scissors, they do it remembering God in their hearts. But one should not misunderstand that they are worshipping the profession itself.

Such customs have come into all religions. The reason for that is the paths discovered by our ancestors were not insignificant. Those who came later saying that the moon and the sun are gods did so either to mislead ignorant people or because they themselves were misguided. Otherwise, no one has ever said that they are gods.

Because the Treta Yuga and Dvapara Yuga were the times of the Devas, these Devas themselves have been depicted even as God and Brahman. Since it was the era of the Devas back then, such things would happen. But after entering this Kali Yuga, in order to repeatedly bring about the Kali Yuga, God very carefully brought forth various great souls (Mahatmas). Then He would create several people as their followers. No matter how they are created and brought forth, some people will hold on to the old ways and act in opposition. Truly, it cannot be said to be their fault. Because they have a familiarity with what they have been practicing. Beyond that, there is a caution in the subtle world that one should not transcend this status of the Devas. From demons to the Trimurti, everyone maintains that caution.

It is said in Islam that the kingdom is ruled by Raja Jinns. In fact, that is correct. It happens in such a way that if a person is born with purity, capability, and competence akin to the deities, this subtle power will align with him and make him operate it. To keep someone with considerable intelligence, capability, and competence at that level and prevent them from progressing, an ego is imparted to them. It instills an ego in him, making him think, "I am the ruler," or "I am intelligent," or "I possess knowledge and wealth—I am competent." However, a person who possesses all these things never gets the wisdom to think: "Oh God! You have given me so much intelligence and capability, but I am not worthy of any of this. What is the state of my body and mind? What significance does my capability have? What will I become if I lose my consciousness the next moment, or what will happen to me if my body is afflicted with an incapacity or disease? What have I achieved in my lineage?" If one has wisdom, one should think in this direction as well, cultivate a more grounded nature, and combine humility, strength, and logic to attain the fortune of finding completeness through karma. How many of us have preserved this? No one has. Because of this, we have incurred numerous shortcomings.

The previously mentioned specific power known as the 'subtle world' (sookshma lokam) is indeed the individual souls (jivatmas) themselves. Remaining there, just as the rays of the sun and the moon fall, its rays too are constantly falling. It will initially approach those jivatmas who possess a virtuous mindset among the virtuous. However, when he seeks to progress towards liberation (mukti) or the status of a deity, he will be obstructed there. This has been the experience of all the great souls who have existed to date. When such an obstruction occurs, no matter how great he is, his mind will be diverted and shift towards something else. Alternatively, if his merit (punya) is immense enough to transcend his fortune and innate nature, he might be inflicted with an ego capable of destroying that merit. Thus, certain phenomena exist within this subtle realm.

You might harbor doubts regarding whether all these things truly exist. They certainly do exist. Nothing that is non-existent has a name in this world. However, the great souls have already provided us with evidence demonstrating that humanity holds a position beyond all this and that humans are capable of overcoming all these obstacles.
Letters Sent to Indira Gandhi
July-August 1984

(The purpose of sending this letter is not merely for the Indian; it is written and sent to integrate the human life that currently exists, has passed, and is yet to come across the entire world, serving as an ultimate example or life, for the continuous effort towards the foundational step. Regardless of who among you opens this, if you feel that you are not entitled to pass it on, you should not tear it up or throw it in the dustbin. You must at least keep it with yourself. Alternatively, if you feel inclined to deliver it happily, it is desired that you execute this with the conviction that you and others will achieve through individual karma. Following this, a letter will be sent every week.)
With love,
Your Swami
To the attention of the loving Mother,

To fully justify addressing you as 'Mother', one's karma must indeed be pure. This letter is written with the aspiration that by earning complete merit to become not only a model for us Indians but for the entire world, and an inexhaustible wealth for the nation, it may serve as the foundation for us, the Mother who is with us, and the world.

According to our Hindu logic, the origin of humanity is considered to be through the lineage of Manu. That is also our knowledge. The Trinity (Trimurti) has also entered our worship in the meantime. Today, we can observe that the entire world is eagerly striving for something. If observed closely, it is evident that not only humans but all living beings are yearning for something. Everything is intended for the good. If we think with a little intelligence, we can understand without anyone telling us how Manu and his lineage, concerning India, have operated and culminated in the rightful state of renunciation (sannyasa), effectively demonstrating the sum total of such an intention. The evidence for this is that India established better universities (Nalanda, Takshashila) than anywhere else in the world. Due to their karmic proficiency, we are still accustomed to boasting about them by name. However, the purpose of this is to create an opportunity to think together about how much it is possible for us to experience this today, rather than it merely shining like the Milky Way of poets.

The purpose of these brief words is to instill the enthusiasm to firmly reflect upon the successes and failures we confront today, and to act with foresight, bestowing a purity upon our successors, the younger generation, with love and respect. The awareness that we are functioning in accordance with the times is contained within us for this purpose. The opportunity to state here that believers, as children of the world, must know things in accordance with the times was created for a specific understanding. Today, the entire world believes this to be the Kali Yuga.

In this Kali Yuga, most people hold the assumption that the world will be destroyed. Even if we merely consult the calculations of our epics regarding the existence of the world, or the calculations of other nations, upon realizing the reality, the calculation is that this is the seventh Manvantara since the origin of the world, and seven more Manvantaras are yet to come. Currently, the Vaivasvata Manvantara is progressing. Within it, the Kali Yuga, which is the fourth quarter of the twenty-eighth Chaturyuga, is taking place. In this Kali Yuga, human life and the objective of governance should harmonize with a steadfast detachment to act and direct actions towards the impending Satya Yuga. This should be done with the Shudras, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Brahmanas working together, and all humans acting with the thought of one faith, one love, and one religion, ensuring that by the time the Satya Yuga arrives, the absolute wisdom of the sages, the absolute karmic proficiency of the deities, and the absolute prophets or the absolute eminent renunciates—with the conviction that their pure lives have perpetually materialized in karma among the people. We must also possess the firm conviction that governance can, to a certain extent, participate in shaping an ideal life.

In this regard, the government must understand and act in accordance with the times. To comprehend this, we must know the successes and failures of the yuga dharmas that our predecessors repeatedly engaged in. If one does not act with this knowledge, there is a proverb among sannyasis: "If it comes, let it come, otherwise only a thread is lost." If one can tie a thread to a mountain and pull it close, that is a victory. Otherwise, only the tied thread and time are lost. The meaning of the phrase "if it comes, let it come" implies acting in sync with time. If it aligns with time, even this thread is unnecessary; one merely needs to push it along with the current. The reason it is advised to tie the thread of karma is that if it is merely pushed, when the flow ceases, it will sink here and there in the water. The thread is meant to keep it afloat and steady without hitting obstacles. Today, we have completely obtained the flow. All that remains for us is to swim upwards in that flow, aiming at the goal. How fortunate we are to have received the opportunity for the swim of karma to fully succeed. It is the Mother's fortune—or rather, our fortune—that an opportunity has arisen to act as the central pillar of the government, to act by honoring, observing, and understanding with absolute love and respect that great power, Ishvara, God, Brahman, Parabrahman, that truth which represents any invocation based on respective religions, which provided the opportunity for our birth and our fortune. Saluting with silent, profound nectar our fortune of getting the opportunity to act by glorifying, praising, and extolling with perfect encomiums, and offering salutations to the Mother, who is the first step in acquiring the courage to act eternally by accepting the medium of prostration with a bowed head, and to a capacity for action like that of the Mother,
Your Swami
To the attention of the loving Mother,

Let us believe that the purpose and objective have been understood from what was previously stated. There is ample evidence here regarding where we experienced shortcomings and vulnerabilities in properly understanding and executing these actions. The truth is that we have not been able to examine even one of these and rectify the flaw. Many great souls have pointed out the medium through which we should act for this. Some are also seen acting upon it. Only those who acted in accordance with the times are seen advancing among them. At the forefront of this are Moses, Jesus, and the Prophet, and their lineage. Long before that, it was Krishna who proved certain matters to us with guidance. Sri Krishna Paramatman proved through his own life that he had to incarnate in that state because numerous rights and wrongs occurred not only to India but to the world due to the actions of many great souls even before that. There is absolutely no doubt that this was demonstrated for our sake, for the sake of foresight. That divine resolve desires to be implemented through various means like this. Pertaining to certain aspects that compel us towards this, those who first erred and caused errors effectively destroyed their own *karma*. *Karma* here means the body. The proof that the divine resolve had foreseen this in some way long before is the very fact that the Yadava family possessed royal status. The valor of Kamsa, who was depicted as an aggressor by history regardless of whether he was actually one or not, is illustrated. By being born as a small child in it, showcasing a long period of aggressive tendencies through the child's biography, destroying it through life or *karma*, and demonstrating through the eighteen divisions of war *karma* what appropriate and practical efficiency should exist in that place, it serves as a supreme example for us to proceed as the successors of that *karma*. Krishna's life showed what is needed and what is not needed in that position by completely annihilating the eighteen *Akshauhini* army, which included Bhishma, Shalya, and others known as gurus and elders until then. Not only did we fail to attain it, but we have also experienced the consequences of tearing apart and destroying that life. We are well aware that the consequence of not obeying it, or the consequence of not having that path proven to us, is that the Kohinoor diamond, which was the greatest adornment for a royal title at that time, adorned the imperial title of the British. Even before that, the Mughals came and took the Shiva Linga gem, which we believe to be one of the greatest in our worship, and kept it as a stepping stone in their place of worship. If it appears that we are believers in God, because our ancestors' undertaking was incorrect, one diverted worship; the other diverted the government. As a result of those who grew up in the ice through history becoming ready for a struggle capable of overturning the world itself through effort, we carry out their activities today under the name of black sahibs. Let us not forget the reality that we can learn certain disciplines only if we use their language itself.

It has been proven so far that it has not been possible religiously, politically, or administratively to advance by taking the past systems, whether right or wrong, in this manner. There is absolutely no doubt that if we cannot change or rewrite this calamity that the world is facing today, our country will also reach the brink of a massive catastrophe. Like Krishna and the Prophet, the *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam* (the twelve clans born of a Pariah woman) here have demonstrated many things. Many things have been shown in such a way as to make the position of a deity seem like a mere farce. It does not mean that there is no deity. It is not meant to say that there is no god, goddess, or subordinate deities in the Trinity worship. For the epoch of *Kali*, the deity itself took birth as a human, displaying the functions of a deity, sage, and ascetic, and to make the intrinsic values of it useful to humanity through a lineage of gurus or prophets, the government, the Vedic system, and as religious believers trusting in it, the Vedic scholar, the pundit, and the associated skilled practitioners must unite, reflect on what the guidance for it is, find guidance suitable for these times, and learn the lacking matters from a wise one (Jnani). Today, we have at our disposal a medium that is possible through a wise one who knows the past, future, and present through realization. We can know it through such a path. Just as in the instance where Krishna is said to have revealed it to Arjuna, and like the medium spoken of by the Prophet—it is said that I received it through words, light, and form proven to us—which became experiential for us in later times; the Prophet's words back then that deserts would be seen as cities and that endless gems and various minable resources could be excavated from this soil have been fulfilled today. Similarly, as long as this remains experiential for us, the time has long passed for us to act with the conviction that our country and our government can only survive through knowledgeable people. Towards this, create an opportunity for the government, believers, devotees, and the renunciates to work together. Attempt to unify the followers of all religions. Call upon the wise ones who can perfectly explain the three dimensions of time in this, or go to them, ask and learn how to handle it, understand both the past and the present, and believe and make others believe in a path that guides towards what is to come. In this, we can only trust the words of the wise ones. There is absolutely no doubt that scholars and the government, by trusting the words of such wise ones and acting upon them, adopting it as a medium, can bring about a correction for the world. As a witness or knowledge to this, the notification that we, as a lineage, can correct it behind the word of God, conveys that word to you. That word is as noted below.
The knowledge or celestial voice we received in 1973—the word from the light—the notification from the form—

'The matter I had desired for epochs has been fulfilled today.' Following that, we are convinced beyond doubt that the notification received until 1984 enables us to know and communicate what the destiny of this world is. We wish to inform you of this in a manner that you can verify and understand using science—the modern science seen today—or through experiments and observations. To utilize your capabilities, ours, and the knowledge of scholars together in a way beneficial to the world, for rulers comparable to a mother, philanthropists, and wise individuals to work unitedly to avert the impending dangerous juncture in the world, and for the children of the world to find and live with peace and harmony behind it, allow us to convey these words.

Today, there are two groups of people in the world: believers and non-believers. Regardless of which group one belongs to, we are all convinced that, apart from certain routines of life, human life is essentially the same for everyone. Furthermore, apart from the fact that life is led according to the nature of each country and human intellect, no other difference is seen. In this regard, concerning India, most people in the world tend to believe that it is a symbol of peace. The reason for this is the diligence and efficiency of our past ancestors. This has mostly come through the lineage of preceptors (Acharyas) and intellectuals. Although some excellent words are highlighted in it, it can only be said that a traditional mistake has occurred, which we have not been able to practice and maintain. But if asked, we can explain it. We possess that knowledge. The government must be completely attentive to imparting such knowledge into human life, especially into the lives of young children, both boys and girls. The government should prepare a scheme that can be implemented by some public servants without any religious discrimination, and execute it in every home to make parents aware of combining education and culture to make life value-based. This will make the motherhood and fatherhood of the children growing up in it valuable. They will never have the tendency seen today of destroying universities. The heinous act of quarreling by citing a long list of sects in the name of religion or caste will not be seen. The true path to achieving this would be to work behind the ideas of the wise, guided by their blessings and instructions, which will act as a support and shade for the good intentions formed by the unity of political and religious followers. Merely citing past myths and epics will not be enough for this. Only a wise person (Jnani) who knows the present and the future can handle this. The government must have the resolve to believe this and make people believe it. For this, we have now achieved an excellent time for the government to bring together all good and efficient people to work. Looking forward to drawing the attention of mother-like administrators and efficient workers towards this,
Your Swami
Guruvani
September 1984

Today, in this Kali Yuga, the one called a Brahmin has become a Chandala, and the one called a Shudra has become a Brahmin. However, even today, the Shudra has no position in Tamil Nadu. Yet, the descendants of those who were Shudras here possess great abilities. But despite attaining that ability, since they did not embrace Brahmanhood, that lineage has suffered degradation today. If you examine each instance like this, you will see that they are not taking it up.

It was the one at the lowest rung who was given it first. From the 'Parayi Petta Panthirukulam' (the twelve tribes born to a Pariah woman) to the eighteen Siddhars, they were brought and tested. Most of these eighteen Siddhars belonged to the Shudra class. That is how God will reveal it to you. In Western countries too, it was brought through a Shudra. Through Jesus—who came from perfect fishermen.

Similarly, among the Arabian people, the birth of the Prophet was as the son of a carpenter belonging to the lowest stratum—one who made and sold idols. You can ponder why God maintained such a contradictory attitude. It is proof that this is the era of the Shudra. Not only here, but everywhere God has brought it this way. You do not understand that. You are again trying to search upwards. You are not reflecting on the fact that it has come down from above.

In recent times, Sree Narayana Guru and Chattampi Swami were born in two communities here. You did not imbibe anything they preached. Each of you has deviated from the path of becoming a Brahmin and is in a rush to show off your strength through wealth, education, and power. None of this aligns with God's desire. Therefore, it is despised by God.

Today in Kerala, the Nair community is considered to be one of the most logical and administratively skilled. Observe if anything else remains in them other than this initial bravado. You need to think very deeply about this. If anything happens, they will exaggerate it and show it as something huge. They will do whatever it takes for that. But they will not do anything with true inner understanding. If you look at their temple traditions, they will do everything externally—building it, performing poojas, coming to pray, and showing rituals. After showing all this, when it comes to the matter of the inner pooja, everyone steps back. They do not take up the Vedic practices either. They are also unable to personally call upon God to eradicate the afflictions in their lineage.

But in today's times, do not think that God has brought all this to test and know us. It is not testing that is being done. Five thousand years have passed since the Kali Yuga began for us now. Although it seems like a long duration, it is only a short period. Dvapara Yuga is double the duration of Kali Yuga. Treta Yuga is double that of Dvapara Yuga. But Satya Yuga is as long as all these three combined. Thus, after the passage of such a long period, God caused the birth of individuals to bring about a transformation here. Even then, improvements were made through individuals. It was them we called prophets or gurus. Apart from through them, we have achieved nothing here to this day. The mediums that have come through their path are temples, churches, and ashrams. The one called a prophet is, in truth, a guru.

As I have said before, in ancient times, when there was no knowledge regarding art, if some scribble was drawn, it was considered art. As it evolved, people learned to draw the human figure with complete beauty. Adding colors and decorations to it, they began carving it on stone and earth. Later, they also started worshiping it, calling it a deity. When a little more beauty was added, it felt like God. After that, the figures of men and women were decorated and sculpted. I am talking about the early humans of the Stone Age. In those days, no one in the forest used to wear clothes. They did not know about clothing. That is why when the pictures of people of that time (men and women) were carved, they were nude figures. As time passed, they started covering just a few parts. This is because the changes brought into their art reflected how they gradually started wearing clothes according to their civilization. You can see all this if you look.

In recent times, all the gods in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka got mustaches. Similarly, if you look at the depictions of women referred to as Menaka, Rambha, and Tilottama, these nylon sarees flow over them. They are painted in such a way that it seems they wore all this back then. In this manner, all forms of knowledge that God has given us to this day have been through humans.
Guruvani
October 1984

There is an art to Sanyasa (asceticism). What is called the art of Sanyasa is filled with immense merit and love. Most people do not have any idea about it. That is no one's fault either. The past two Yugas were times that highly praised, knew, and proclaimed the era of the Devas. In this Kali Yuga, which has lasted only five thousand years, the things spoken by various great souls and prophets at different times have only partially reached our ears. It may have reached a few people according to their respective merits. There are many who hear and dismiss it. However, this is not a time to dismiss it, but to pay attention. Within these five thousand years, a section of people who were considered the most inexperienced and uncultured have ruled and come forward. But even though efforts were made for the smooth administration of the country or the world, they have not been successful. However, the time for it to be sufficiently successful is now. It is God's decree that it must happen through humans.

Without understanding this divine will, what all are our people still doing today! Worshipping Bhadrakali, their attitude is 'I will show the greatness of my Goddess'. Bringing all kinds of 'absurdities' through these rituals, and intertwining our very lives in them, we have degraded ourselves to such an extent that we do not even desire the survival of the soul. When speaking of the survival of the soul, being born as a human itself is for the achievement of the soul. A soul attains a human birth only after millions of past lives. Human birth is the most supreme among all births. Getting a male birth is even more supreme. A birth as a devotee is even more distinguished than that. Therefore, we can achieve immense fulfillment through a human life. It is the flaw of not evaluating and reflecting upon this that, despite the advent of Mahatmas (great souls) all this time, it has not been of proper use to us. What was revealed through the divine message here is that two thousand four hundred and forty-four Mahatmas were caused to be born in the Kali Yuga itself. Even though so many great souls were born in the Kali Yuga, the shortcomings of the people could not be resolved.

As an example of the aforementioned shortcoming – after we are born, grow up, and lead a moderate householder's life (*Grihasthashrama*), the subsequent period is the time to earn something for the soul. However, if we examine each individual's life, we see that their householder life extends until the end of their life. Once a person leads a householder's life and their children have grown up—regardless of the good or bad that befalls them—the logic of staying back to raise and reform them, their children, and their children's children, instead of seeking the path to spiritual liberation (*Jivanmukti*), is incomprehensible. Their entire lifetime is spent raising children, and then they depart. They have neither seen anything beyond this nor do they possess any other thought. Those who pass their time thinking, "If I could just get this youngest daughter married off, I could have taken *Sannyasa*," will not feel like stepping away even after getting that youngest daughter's daughter married. Then they realize the elder son's daughter's child is ready for marriage. The thought would be, "It would not be a bad idea to die after seeing her married off as well." In this manner, getting continuously entangled, they have absolutely no concern for their own souls. We need nothing else for our downfall in this state—we ourselves become the cause of it. This is the meaning behind the saying that one will lie bound in the cycle of birth and death like a cartwheel.

Saying this does not mean that you should not rejoice upon seeing your own children. There are lessons these children must learn over time by observing the lives of this grandfather, grandmother, father, and mother. When that happens, they will reflect, "The same status that my predecessor lived and demonstrated is sufficient for me." Thus, this is a good method to prevent bequeathing ruin to the world.

You led a comfortable life. Yet, for the comfort of your children and their children, you live with the attitude of "making money even by stabbing another to death." You have no time to reflect on what purpose this serves. Whenever one looks, there are only some forms of money-making schemes and debts. Beyond this, you are unable to earn anything else. How many generations backward will the progeny of one who hoards excessively in this manner regress? Will not the entire karmic consequence of what was acquired through wicked means be transmitted to them as well? We should not allow ourselves to be ruined in this manner. This does not mean wealth is unnecessary. While alive, one must not stretch out one's hand to beg from any human being. For that, one must certainly work hard through a righteous path, eat properly, and earn wealth. Only then will our children also turn out the same way.

Today, the children of householders who return from Persia (the Gulf) have a certain way of walking about for a few days. They are seen in a state where they have no idea how to drape their clothes or how to walk. It is mostly seen in the Varkala region. Chirayinkeezhu taluk is the most prominent for it. They do not even know how the wealth they earn should be utilized. If handled in this manner, what will become of their next generation! Such impoverished children will eventually disappear from sight. They will commit any kind of robbery. Having acquired a little education as well, they will completely ruin the land. They will turn into such vile individuals. Therefore, such householders must be extremely cautious. All this stems from their ignorance. This is because they have not lived in the correct manner. Therefore, when they get a few pennies, they show this arrogance, thinking they will not be considered smart unless they create a commotion over it. A nature that rectifies all this ignorance must emerge through our lineage itself.
Guruvani
November 1984

Generally, there is an ignorance seen among those leading a householder's life (*Grihasthashrama*), being unable to know how to conduct their lives. By introducing all sorts of 'absurdities' into our worship practices, we have degraded ourselves to an extent where we do not even desire the survival of the soul. It was mentioned earlier that being born as a human itself is for the achievement of the soul, isn't it? The Kali Yuga is an apt time to rectify all this. The task God has undertaken by causing Mahatmas to be born for that purpose, and correcting all this through their lineage, is no small feat.

Today, there is a competition among householders—between those who go to Arab countries to earn money to live, and those who live here with a small job. One group thinks, "My children, with this small job, must become greater than the others." Another group arrogantly thinks, "I was a mere spade-worker, but look at my children—isn't my money greater than his job?" In this manner, they exhibit arrogance. Remember that if you run competitively like this, you will fall somewhere. It is because of our ignorance that we are running frantically like this. We have not been able to impart any such knowledge to the women in our homes. One reason for that is our very lack of tradition.

It was mentioned earlier that this is the era of the Shudra. It is among them that this commotion has arisen. Ignorance is the reason for its occurrence. Today is a time when the Brahmin has become a Chandala (outcaste), and in that position, the Shudra has been able to become a Brahmin. The *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam* (the twelve clans born to the Pariah woman) and the Eighteen Siddhars are proof of that. After that, distinct Mahatmas were caused to be born among each caste. The reason for that is, only if born in such a way would culture emerge among them. Otherwise, they would be rejected citing their caste. We can attain merit from the birth of a Mahatma only if there is an absence of arrogance. Narayana Guru Swami and Chattampi Swami belong to the group of Mahatmas who came in that manner. At the time of their birth—for both these groups—anyone with a few pennies did not want them. It was only poor and uneducated people who accepted them. Because of that, they improved to a certain extent.

Sri Narayana Guru Swami contracted a marriage from Anchuthengu. Adjacent to it, in Kayikkara, to the north of Asannagar, there is a household named Perunthara. They were exceedingly wealthy. There was even a colloquial saying among the locals that if the wealth of the Perunthara family were cast into the sea, it would fill the ocean. However, it is innumerable how many destitute children have emerged from such a household. We must reflect upon the underlying reasons for such an occurrence. During those times, they did not accept Narayana Guru Swami. Kakkakuzhi Padmanabhan Vaidyar belonged to this lineage. He was the one who, in opposition to Narayana Guru Swami, appeared before the Travancore Praja Sabha (Legislative Assembly) and argued against 'Temple Entry'. This is being articulated so that you yourselves may reflect upon the extent of degradation and the decline of cultural refinement amidst yourselves. When spiritual masters manifest among you, they are seldom revered. We must cultivate the wisdom and cultural refinement necessary to honor them. To achieve this, virtuous and meritorious children must be born in our midst. Virtuous progeny will be conceived only if there is '*Pithrushuddhi*' (ancestral purification). Accordingly, to rectify these circumstances and to forge a lineage endowed with wisdom and cultural refinement, the Divine has bestowed upon us a profound knowledge. It is towards this noble objective that we are striving here today.

Not merely Sankaracharya, Jesus, or the Prophet, but none of the great souls who have incarnated hitherto have been vested with the authority to perform '*Pithrushuddhi*'. All of them accomplished '*Pithrushuddhi*' merely on a minuscule scale, and that too through immense effort. For this purpose, the followers of Jesus solely engage in rituals such as chanting 'Anatha' for '*Pithrushuddhi*'. Within the tradition of the Prophet, Muslims facilitate sacred rituals such as 'Ratib'. Hindus orchestrate rituals like *Balitharpanam* or *Homam*, and in the temple tradition, '*Kshetrapindam*'. Beyond these practices, a comprehensive methodology for ancestral liberation has not existed until now. That is precisely what we have been granted here. It is impossible to articulate the profound reverence that an individual who truly comprehends the magnitude of this blessing would exhibit.

You might have heard of the term *Bhagiratha Prayathnam* (Herculean effort). It is narrated that Bhagiratha, who had attained such an exalted royal status, renounced it all and undertook penance for an extensive period solely to purify his ancestors. However, in stark contrast, we have been bestowed with a remarkably effortless path here. By merely mandating the performance of a *Gurupooja*, one gazes into the divine light, visualizes the ancestor situated in that realm, and grasps them spiritually. Once grasped, the ancestor is either liberated, retained in the ancestral state, or granted ultimate salvation (*Mukthi*). Liberation in this context implies the granting of a new birth. Consequently, ancestors who receive this rebirth will reincarnate amidst us. Since these ancestors have attained liberation through this profound process, those progeny will be born with extraordinary merit. This spiritual undertaking transcends any caste or religion. Unprecedented in global history, no preceptor has hitherto attained such a divine methodology. The wisdom that manifests through the offspring born in this manner will unequivocally surpass any knowledge we currently exercise. It will exist on a remarkably elevated plane. However, we shall only bear witness to this manifestation when they attain at least thirty years of age.

It has been merely eleven years since we were granted the divine sanction to perform *Pithrushuddhi* in this manner. From that juncture onwards, we have been executing this sacred duty. It is explicitly to acquire such sublime merit within this lineage of descendants that you are instructed to abstain from extraneous modes of worship. If you nurture the ensuing generation that emerges in this manner, your own spiritual deficiencies will be expiated through them. As long as this *Guruparampara* (Guru lineage) endures, your soul shall continue to accrue spiritual merit. Through your divine supplication, your life force and physical vessel accrue sanctity, while simultaneously, your lineage of descendants ascends to an exalted state of merit. Through this profound qualification, what we have ensured is the very preservation of the world. Such an exceptionally monumental spiritual endeavor is what we are undertaking here. While engaging in an action that accumulates such profound spiritual merit, we will inevitably have to endure manifold hardships, tribulations, and sacrifices. If such trials were absent, we would fail to comprehend its intrinsic value.

If one examines the histories of Jesus or the Prophet—what immense sacrifices they endured! Those who placed their faith in them were battered to death! They were crucified! That is precisely what the Crusades exemplify. Hardships accompany only virtuous pursuits; malevolence encounters no such resistance. However, we are not necessitated to endure such monumental sacrifices. Upon conducting a comparative analysis of these two realities, one recognizes how infinitely superior our path is. Therefore, we who are obligated to live revering this path, must cultivate a lifestyle perfectly aligned with its sanctity. That is the imperative duty before us.
Guru Vani
December 1984

Householders (*Grihasthashramis*) are incapable of preserving a spiritual lineage. They can solely protect their offspring. The term lineage, in this context, refers not to biological succession, but to the *Guruparampara* (Guru lineage). Nevertheless, the householder possesses the inherent right to provide the requisite support and sustenance to that spiritual lineage. Jesus introduced a novel system of worship. When individuals placed their faith in it, their lineage prospered. Through the worship paradigm introduced by the Prophet, that lineage also flourished. Buddha similarly introduced a system of worship to this land. However, precisely when it began to flourish, the Brahmins, establishing their stronghold here, methodically corrupted and compromised its descendants. Consequently, the progeny and women within that tradition were subjected to moral decay. As a direct result, Buddhism was compelled to depart from this land. It was the entrenched presence of this caste-based hierarchy here that necessitated its expulsion. All of this was systematically orchestrated utilizing the Shudras as instruments.

Observe the myriad pathways the Divine has manifested for you across various realms. Yet, you fail to embrace them. If, despite being provided with such profound opportunities, you continue to reject them, it will inevitably culminate in natural calamities. Thereafter, no remedial action will be viable. The spiritual legacy we have inherited today is sanctified and everlasting. The prophetic revelation associated with this states: "If we pray with unwavering devotion and humility, the initial manifestation within the next fourteen years will be a monumental political transformation." Concurrently, religious scholars and adherents will inherently begin to undergo a paradigm shift. These religious adherents, having transformed, will be compelled to transition into a realm where they actively seek out genuine virtue. Precisely when politicians, consumed by internecine conflicts, begin to discard their ideologies as futile, a new generation will arise, actively seeking genuine rectitude. This resurgence will emanate from the foundational grassroots level. This phenomenon will subsequently catalyze a global transformation. It is prayer and profound intention (*Sankalpa*) that prepare us for this impending reality. We shall be able to witness firsthand how that prayer comes to fruition here. By spiritually grasping your ancestor and invoking them to this plane, they ascend towards the Divine, propelled by the very prayer you offer from your position. Upon their return, the divine grace permeates into your karmic realm. This process will systematically agitate the afflictions deeply rooted in your life force, fundamentally altering your very character, and gradually, albeit slowly, transform everything. However, this process necessitates a minimum gestation period of twelve years. Occasionally, it may demand the entirety of your lifetime. In the interim, we will be obligated to endure multifarious hardships, adversities, and sacrifices. Do not harbor any fear towards these tribulations. One must inevitably endure slight hardships prior to the manifestation of profound goodness. We must cultivate an unshakeable resolve that states: "Irrespective of the circumstances, I am prepared to endure anything for the sake of my future lineage. I shall make any requisite sacrifice to nurture and elevate my succeeding generation. I require neither personal abode nor homeland, but my lineage must be unequivocally secure."

That is why the story of Bhagiratha was mentioned earlier. He threw away the rule of the kingdom and went to perform penance. Agastya also did the same to purify his ancestors (pitru). When we consider the hardships and sacrifices these figures endured to purify their ancestors, the path God has given us is much simpler and greater. This is not about acquiring supernatural powers (siddhi) or imparting profound knowledge. Yet, it is the very essence of knowledge. There is no other path for anyone on earth. Even after receiving such a noble path, instead of internalizing and practicing it properly, you are always preoccupied with thoughts of whether the husband is qualified, whether the wife is qualified, or whether there is wealth. Whatever that may be, we must fervently pray and embrace this significant opportunity we have received. You must pray with such determination, envisioning that your prayer is capable of wiping away the vileness of this world. Thus, your prayers will provide great support and shelter to this world.

All of that can be seen by your children and by yourselves—those who have the vision to see. Today, there are no less than fifty such individuals in this lineage. If one of our children attains spiritual vision, even the Holy Trinity (Trimurti) would bow before them before departing. That is its state. Narayana Guru Swami said exactly this regarding it—at the pinnacle of philosophical inquiry, one sees everything as one.
Everything we see is the light of this oneness. Therefore, such a supreme thing is what we have obtained.

Here, the Shudras have not had an institution until today. Shudras outside have had them. Both the Prophet and Jesus were Shudras. The term Shudra refers to the Shudra among the four varnas. Thus, the Shudras outside prospered. Those here have not been able to survive. You are standing under the Chandal-like Brahmins. In Kali Yuga, the Brahmin is a Chandala. Brahmins who neither drink alcohol nor lie are rare today. If you look in the Palakkad district, houses among them without insanity and leprosy are rare. They have been rendered Chandalas in that manner. However, God has bestowed prosperity upon the Shudras. Within 25 years, the community affectionately called 'Harijans' by Gandhiji in recent times will develop a culture greater than yours. The Ayyankali Memorial in Kerala is an example of this. The absence of arrogance in them was the foundation of their growth. Although a little arrogance has crept into them today, God will tolerate it. This is because it happened out of their ignorance, not out of defiance. But today, God has already given them a position.

However, there are two groups who refuse to agree to anything. They are the Ezhavas and the Nairs. Generally, the Ezhavas display arrogance and foolishness. Even today, they have the habit of having a full drink poured and saying, 'My Swami, just a little more.' The Nairs are not like that. If you go to Neyyattinkara and observe, even if they have nothing to eat, they will wrap a towel around their neck and walk with regal pomp. You have degenerated to this level. There is no visible effort among you to change all this. It is not that you need asceticism (sannyasa), but rather the capability to live. The first step towards that is the purification of the ancestors. It is because of the lack of this that you put on all these acts. When children are born while the ancestral spirits are astray, they will be inclined to do even worse.

This is a lineage empowered by God to rectify this. Therefore, celibates (brahmacharis) are necessary to lead this. Otherwise, the institution will not survive as it grows. You may speak grandly. But if you do not like it, you will step out and say something else. Will the descendants of such people look after the institution later? Then will the institution you built survive? This is why it is said that the institution of the Shudra does not endure. They build many institutions. The Shudra lacks the diplomacy for this. Rights and wrongs will occur. One must work through them instead of dismissing them with blame.

Have you not seen 'Sivagiri' now? What terrible things are being said from the outside. But see if there is anyone willing to work for it for 4 days. They will only go if there is profit. Isn't Chempazhanthy located nearby? How many people look after it? Other than strutting around and conducting festivals just to ensure 'let our names also be included,' what else do you have? Chenkottukonam is being built up, isn't it? What do you have to maintain there traditionally? However, at Abhedananda Ashram, you have formed a committee in such a way that it is impossible for him to stay there. Today, he merely comes and goes occasionally. Will anyone other than someone with a slight caste feeling remain among you?

You must not bring this lineage to that state. No one should mock the lineage you bring forth. Rights and wrongs will occur within it. You, who are householders, must try to resolve them yourselves. This is your time.

If you do not respect and uphold this, it will slip from your hands. Then some natural disaster or something else will come and destroy everything. Do not allow that to happen. Our efforts must be directed towards preventing that.
Guruvani
